mission_05: Reptile, introduced by Nichol et al. (2018), is a first-order approximation of MAML that is much simpler to implement and computationally cheaper. While MAML computes second-order gradients (differentiating through the inner loop), Reptile simply moves the meta-parameters toward the task-adapted parameters: theta <- theta + eps(theta' - theta), where theta' is obtained by running standard SGD on a task. This update rule has a beautiful interpretation: Reptile maximizes the expected inner product between gradients of different tasks, encouraging parameters that are simultaneously good for many tasks. The algorithm is: (1) sample a task, (2) run SGD on that task for several steps to get theta', (3) update theta toward theta'. Despite its simplicity, Reptile performs competitively with MAML on few-shot learning benchmarks.
